The seven prophetic Old Testament items that are TEXT_PRESENT in Henry Barclay Swete’s The Old Testament in Greek according to the Septuagint (Vol. III: Hosea—4 Maccabees, Cambridge, 1894) are converted below into primary-evidence rows.
P03F-P001
Proposed Evidence ID: P03F-P001
Source ID: P03F
B001 ID: B001-2 (Romans 9:25)
Witness Role: OLD_GREEK
Passage Reference: Ὡσηὲ (Hosea) 2:23 [LXX 2:25]
Exact Source Text: καὶ σπερῶ αὐτὴν ἐμαυτῷ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἀγαπήσω τὴν Οὐκ ἠγαπημένην, καὶ ἐρῶ τῷ Οὐ λαῷ μου Λαός μου εἶ σύ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐρεῖ Κύριος ὁ θεός μου εἶ σύ.
1
Printed Page / Locator: Page 3
1
NotebookLM Citation:
1
Apparatus Present: YES
1
Apparatus Reading(s) & Witnesses: 23 αγαπησω] ελεησω AQ | ηγαπημενην] ηλεημενην AQ
1
.
Textual Feature Relevant to Later Comparison: In the base uncial (Codex Vaticanus, B), the verbs and participles read ἀγαπήσω and ἠγαπημένην, matching the vocabulary of Romans 9:25 (τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην ἠγαπημένην), whereas Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Marchalianus (Q) read ἐλεήσω and ἠλεημένην
1
. The citation clause itself is framed as direct address (καὶ ἐρῶ τῷ Οὐ λαῷ μου Λαός μου εἶ σύ), differing from Paul's accusative construction (Καλέσω τὸν οὐ λαόν μου λαόν μου)
1
.
Limitation of This Source: Supplies only the Greek uncial witnesses (B, A, Q); it does not supply the Masoretic Hebrew text of Hosea 2:23 [MT 2:25] or the New Testament text of Romans 9:25.
P03F-P002
Proposed Evidence ID: P03F-P002
Source ID: P03F
B001 ID: B001-3 (Romans 9:26)
Witness Role: OLD_GREEK
Passage Reference: Ὡσηὲ (Hosea) 1:10 [LXX 2:1]
Exact Source Text: καὶ ἦν ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης, ἣ οὐκ ἐκμετρηθήσεται οὐδὲ ἐξαριθμηθήσεται· καὶ ἔσται ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς Οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς, κληθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος.
2
Printed Page / Locator: Page 2
2
NotebookLM Citation:
2
Apparatus Present: YES
2
Apparatus Reading(s) & Witnesses: 10 τω τοπω ου sup ras Bab | ερρηθη Q3 | κληθησονται] pr εκει A | om και αυτοι A (s' θ' το και om Qmg)
2
.
Textual Feature Relevant to Later Comparison: While the base text (Codex Vaticanus, B) reads κληθήσονται καὶ αὐτοί, Codex Alexandrinus (A) prefixes ἐκεῖ to κληθήσονται (pr εκει A) and omits καὶ αὐτοί (om και αυτοι A), yielding the exact phrase ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος
2
. The marginal notes of Codex Marchalianus (Qmg) record that Symmachus and Theodotion likewise omit τὸ καί
2
.
Limitation of This Source: Contains only Greek manuscript evidence and Hexaplaric marginal notes; it does not contain the Hebrew text of Hosea 1:10 [MT 2:1] or the Pauline text of Romans 9:26.
P03F-P003
Proposed Evidence ID: P03F-P003
Source ID: P03F
B001 ID: B001-4 (Romans 10:11)
Witness Role: OLD_GREEK
Passage Reference: Ἡσαΐας (Isaiah) 28:16
Exact Source Text: διὰ τοῦτο οὕτως λέγει κύριος Κύριος Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐμβάλλω εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σειὼν λίθον πολυτελῆ ἐκλεκτὸν ἀκρογωνιαῖον ἔντιμον, εἰς τὰ θεμέλια αὐτῆς, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ.
3
Printed Page / Locator: Page 149
3
NotebookLM Citation:
3
Apparatus Present: YES
3
Apparatus Reading(s) & Witnesses: 16 om κς 2° א A Q* (hab Qmg) Γ | εμβαλω א AQ | Σιων Ba?bאAQΓ | αυτής] + ※ τεθεμελιωμενον Qmg | ο πιστευων] + επ αυτω אAQ | ου μη καταισχυνθη] οι γ' (θη sup ras A?vid) ου σπευσει Qmg
3
.
Textual Feature Relevant to Later Comparison: In the target clause, the base text (Codex Vaticanus, B) reads simply καὶ ὁ πιστεύων οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ, but Codex Sinaiticus (א), Codex Alexandrinus (A), and Codex Marchalianus (Q) all explicitly add ἐπʼ αὐτῷ (+ επ αυτω אAQ), demonstrating that the dative prepositional phrase was established in early Greek Old Testament uncial transmission
3
. The apparatus also notes that the Three (Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotion) render the verb as οὐ σπεύσει in Qmg
3
.
Limitation of This Source: Documents only Septuagint uncials and marginal versions; it does not supply the Hebrew text of Isaiah 28:16 or the New Testament text of Romans 10:11.
P03F-P004
Proposed Evidence ID: P03F-P004
Source ID: P03F
B001 ID: B001-5 (Romans 10:13)
Witness Role: OLD_GREEK
Passage Reference: Ἰωὴλ (Joel) 2:32 [LXX 3:5]
Exact Source Text: καὶ ἔσται πᾶς ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου σωθήσεται· ὅτι ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σειὼν καὶ ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἔσται ἀνασωζόμενος, καθότι εἶπεν Κύριος, καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι οὓς Κύριος προσκέκληται.
4
Printed Page / Locator: Page 47
4
NotebookLM Citation:
4
Apparatus Present: YES
4
Apparatus Reading(s) & Witnesses: 32 αν] εαν א | επικαληται א* (-λεσηται אc.a -λησηται אc.b) | Σιων Ba?bאAQ3 | om εν 2° A | ευαγγελισμενος ([-νοι] Q*vid)
4
.
Textual Feature Relevant to Later Comparison: The core quotation clause πᾶς ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου σωθήσεται is supported unanimously by Codex Vaticanus (B), Codex Alexandrinus (A), and Codex Marchalianus (Q)
4
. Codex Sinaiticus (א) displays minor scribal variations (ἐάν for ἄν, and ἐπικαλῆται prima manu)
4
. The Greek text opens with καὶ ἔσται, lacking the Pauline connective particle γάρ (Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν... in Rom 10:13)
4
.
Limitation of This Source: Provides only the Septuagint uncial text; it lacks the Hebrew text of Joel 2:32 [MT 3:5] and the New Testament quotation context of Romans 10:13.
P03F-P005
Proposed Evidence ID: P03F-P005
Source ID: P03F
B001 ID: B001-6 (Romans 11:34)
Witness Role: OLD_GREEK
Passage Reference: Ἡσαΐας (Isaiah) 40:13
Exact Source Text: τίς ἔγνω νοῦν Κυρίου, καὶ τίς αὐτοῦ σύμβουλος ἐγένετο, ὃς συμβιβᾷ αὐτόν;
5
Printed Page / Locator: Page 174
5
NotebookLM Citation:
5
Apparatus Present: YES
5
Apparatus Reading(s) & Witnesses: 13 συμβουλος αυτου AQΓ | συμβιβα] συμβιβασει אc.a (-βασι sed ras σι) AQmgΓ
5
.
Textual Feature Relevant to Later Comparison: While Codex Vaticanus (B) prints αὐτοῦ σύμβουλος, Codex Alexandrinus (A), Codex Marchalianus (Q), and Codex Cryptoferratensis (Γ) read σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ (συμβουλος αυτου AQΓ), aligning exactly with the word order of Romans 11:34 (σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο)
5
. The Greek Old Testament coordinates the questions with καί (καὶ τίς...) and includes a third clause (ὃς συμβιβᾷ αὐτόν;), whereas Paul coordinates with ἤ and omits the final clause
5
.
Limitation of This Source: Supplies only the Septuagint uncial witnesses; it does not provide the Masoretic Hebrew text of Isaiah 40:13 or the New Testament text of Romans 11:34.
P03F-P006
Proposed Evidence ID: P03F-P006
Source ID: P03F
B001 ID: B001-7 (Romans 15:12)
Witness Role: OLD_GREEK
Passage Reference: Ἡσαΐας (Isaiah) 11:10
Exact Source Text: καὶ ἔσται ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἡ ῥίζα τοῦ Ἰεσσαὶ καὶ ὁ ἀνιστάμενος ἄρχειν ἐθνῶν, ἐπʼ αὐτῷ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν· καὶ ἔσται ἡ ἀνάπαυσις αὐτοῦ τιμή.
6
Printed Page / Locator: Page 122

NotebookLM Citation:
6
Apparatus Present: YES
6
Apparatus Reading(s) & Witnesses: 10 εθνω (sic) A
6
.
Textual Feature Relevant to Later Comparison: Unanimous uncial agreement exists across B, א, Q, and Γ for the entire target clause, with Codex Alexandrinus (A) exhibiting an isolated typographical error (εθνω)
6
. The Old Greek text retains the introductory temporal clause ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ, which is absent from Paul's quotation in Romans 15:12 (Ἔσται ἡ ῥίζα τοῦ Ἰεσσαί...)
6
.
Limitation of This Source: Supplies only early Greek uncial witnesses; it does not supply the Hebrew text of Isaiah 11:10 or the Pauline text of Romans 15:12.
P03F-P007
Proposed Evidence ID: P03F-P007
Source ID: P03F
B001 ID: B001-8 (1 Corinthians 1:19)
Witness Role: OLD_GREEK
Passage Reference: Ἡσαΐας (Isaiah) 29:14
Exact Source Text: διὰ τοῦτο ἰδοὺ προσθήσω τοῦ μεταθεῖναι τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον καὶ μεταθήσω αὐτούς, καὶ ἀπολῶ τὴν σοφίαν τῶν σοφῶν, καὶ τὴν σύνεσιν τῶν συνετῶν κρύψω.
7
Printed Page / Locator: Page 152
7
NotebookLM Citation:
7
Apparatus Present: YES
7
Apparatus Reading(s) & Witnesses: 14 ιδου] + εγω א* (improb אc.a) A | αυτους] + μεταθεσει Z | σοφων] + αυτων Z | συνετων] + αυτου Z
7
.
Textual Feature Relevant to Later Comparison: In the target clause, all collated primary uncial witnesses (B, א, A, Q, Z, Γ) unanimously read κρύψω (καὶ τὴν σύνεσιν τῶν συνετῶν κρύψω), with palimpsest Z adding genitive pronouns (σοφῶν + αὐτῶν, συνετῶν + αὐτοῦ)
7
. None of the uncial witnesses exhibit the verb ἀθετήσω, which is printed in 1 Corinthians 1:19
7
.
Limitation of This Source: Documents only the Greek Septuagint textual tradition; it does not contain the Hebrew text of Isaiah 29:14 or the New Testament text of 1 Corinthians 1:19.
